key_insight: Applying orthogonal gradient projection inside a shared LoRA adapter disentangles conflicting task updates by removing gradient components that interfere across tasks, reducing negative transfer while keeping a single, parameter-efficient adapter.
problem_solved: Negative transfer in multi-task LoRA: conflicting gradient updates from different tasks degrade per-task performance when a single LoRA adapter is shared across tasks.
method: Compute task-specific gradient directions within the LoRA low-rank parameter subspace during multi-task training.
Project each task's gradient orthogonally to the subspace spanned by other tasks' conflicting components (Orthogonal Gradient Projection) before applying updates.
Update the shared LoRA adapter with the conflict-free (projected) gradients, preserving low-rank structure and parameter efficiency.
impact: Enables reliable multi-task adaptation with a single LoRA adapter by reducing negative transfer, improving per-task performance while keeping storage and compute benefits of parameter-efficient tuning.
visual_elements: Before/After diagram showing overlapping/conflicting gradient vectors in the adapter subspace vs. orthogonally separated vectors after projection.
Architecture sketch: base LLM + single shared LoRA adapter with a module indicating orthogonal projection per task.
Bar or heatmap comparing per-task performance (single-task fine-tune vs. shared LoRA vs. shared LoRA + OGP).
Algorithm flowchart: compute gradients → build conflict subspace → orthogonal projection → apply updates.
paper_title: Disentangling Task Conflicts in Multi-Task LoRA via Orthogonal Gradient Projection
paper_authors: Ziyu Yang, Guibin Chen, Yuxin Yang, Aoxiong Zeng, Xiangquan Yang
